newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 7.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- A commentary urges film industry be improved and more excellent movies be produced to meet people's needs, urging artists to focus on films with a "mainstream theme."
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- Front-page story covers afforestation, says tree planting should be an important work of the nation as a whole.
- Chinese filmmakers should shoulder responsibility for providing "cultural food" for the people by carrying out a high-profile programme to revive the movie industry.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Editorial warns against overheating of stock market
FINANCIAL NEWS

- Central bank governor Dai Xianglong says financial officials should have sense of responsibility, including strictly controlling money supply and using interest rates and credit tools to promote the economy
- Mao Yingliang, head of central bank Shanghai branch, calls on commercial banks in Shanghai to trim unhealthy loans
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- State Administration of Taxation issues notice to private firms to set up standard accounts from April 1
- China seen cautious in approving BOT projects because of lack of regulations and laws
MARKET DAILY
- Rising official corruption in construction industry and low quality control contribute to rising number of accidents
- China offshore crude output seen exceeding 16 million tonnes in 1997
CHINA DAILY
- Chinese Academy of Sciences has decided to tackle large-scale research projects related to economy in remaining years of the century.
- China's most populous city of Chongqing is planning to clean up its image with ambitious anti-pollution programme.
